body: CC @hippo91 I think we added a fix for this a while back. Maybe @hippo91 could confirm when he gets a chance.

@PCManticore the bugs #1741 and #1742 are related but not exactly the same.
@madeddy thanks a lot. I can reproduce the bug and will work on it ASAP but i'm really busy this moment.

@madeddy in fact disabling ```C0301``` does disable ```line-too-long``` message emission but not in all cases.

I'm linting the following piece of code:

```
#pylint: disable=missing-docstring, C0301

# Hey this is a very long commented line just to trigger pylint's line-too-long message. It is just above a dummy function with a very long code line.
def dummy_function():
    print("What a beautiful dummy function with such a very long line inside it should trigger pylint's line-too-long message ")
```
On my laptop, pylint result is: 
```
No config file found, using default configuration

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 10.00/10 (previous run: 10.00/10, +0.00)
```

Of course if i remove ```C0301``` i get:
```
No config file found, using default configuration
************* Module bug_1950
C:  3, 0: Line too long (150/100) (line-too-long)
C:  5, 0: Line too long (128/100) (line-too-long)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 0.00/10 (previous run: 10.00/10, -10.00)
```

However if i add a long commented line at the end of the module, then i got message emission even if i disabled ```C0301```. I'm working on it.

issue.title: Proposal of a fix for bug #1950

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
The bug arises when a module ends with a long commented line.
This is because the line doesn't appear in the AST and thus is absent from Lint.file_state._module_msgs_state. 
The strategy adopted is to check if the line number is above the maximum line number present in Lint.file_state._module_msgs_state and if it is the case the message emission is deactivated if the msgid C0301 is present in Lint.file_state._raw_module_msgs_state.
I added a unit test that should not emit any messages.

Close #1950

issue.title: long comment or multiline string at end of file isn't ignored properly

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1.  put a long multiline string or a long comment at the end of a file
2. add `line-too-long` to the list of ignored errors in `.pylintrc`
3. run `pylint <file>`

### Current behavior
`line-too-long` error is returned

### Expected behavior
`line-too-long` error should be ignored

### pylint --version output
```shell
> pylint --version
pylint 2.0.1
astroid 2.0.1
Python 3.6.5 (default, May 11 2018, 09:14:55)
[GCC 4.2.1 Compatible Apple LLVM 9.0.0 (clang-900.0.39.2)]
```
Repro'd on 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 releases, the pre-release version as specified in the issue template, as well as master (as of https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/commit/2b24ec063a5355648d286633e37f084ced4f1604)

### Examples
long final comment:
```python
"""Testing long lines."""


print("requires some code before the comment")
# Some really long comment.  No, no, no - MUCH longer than this.  At least 100 chars.  Keep going.  Yeah,
about this long works.
```

really, it's a long comment that isn't followed by more code - it doesn't have to be the last comment:
```python
"""Testing long lines."""


print("requires some code before the comment")
# Some really long comment.  No, no, no - MUCH longer than this.  At least 100 chars.  Keep going.  Yeah,
about this long works.
# The long comment is still caught even if it's not the last line.
```

Long multi-line strings work, too:
```
"""Testing long lines."""


print(
    f"Some really long string.  No, no, no - MUCH longer than this.  At least 100 chars.  Keep going.  Yeah, about this long works."
    f"Some really long string.  No, no, no - MUCH longer than this.  At least 100 chars.  Keep going.  Yeah, about this long works."
)
```

### Similar issue
I found #1950 which was talking about this same problem.  There was investigation, acknowledgement, a fix proposed and merged, and then the issue was closed.

Then it looks like the merged build failed, and the fix was reverted, but the issue was never re-opened.

issue.title: Disabled "line too long"(C0301) not working on docstring comments

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
The following code still generates an error even though "line too long"(C0301) is disabled.

```python
#!/usr/local/bin/python3
"""This is a very long line within a docstring that should trigger a pylint C0301 error line-too-long"""

# pylint: disable=C0301
# pylint: disable=line-too-long
```

Here is the pylint error
```
$ pylint dummy.py 
************* Module dummy
dummy.py:2:0: C0301: Line too long (105/100) (line-too-long)
```

This was talked about previously in issue #1950. The issue was resolved for comments, but it still exists for docstrings.

Using pylint 2.3.1
